newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end higher, gold volume high.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end higher, gold volume high.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended higher across the board Monday, despite a fresh surge in the U.S. dollar overnight, and platinum group metals (PGMs) ended higher despite the resumption of Russian exports this month.
The U.S. dollar surged to a seven-and-a-half-year high against the deutschemark overnight as well as a seven-year high in the U.S. dollar trade weighted index.
"But the rallies in gold and silver still look mostly like short covering by funds and proprietary traders," Refco New York analyst Tim Porter said.
COMEX August gold was settled up $3.00 at $329.50 an ounce, testing the top of the range of the past week around $330.00, ahead of the contract's first notice day Thursday.
The August/December spread widened back out to $4.40 an ounce, now that the roll into the December contract is well advanced.
COMEX December gold, now the more active month, ended up $3.40 at $333.40 an ounce, also testing the top of its range of the past week around $335.00.
December gold's five-day moving average crossed above its 21-day moving average at the close Monday, for the first time since May.

COMEX gold estimated total volume Monday was a solid 78,000 lots, but COMEX gold open interest fell a further 6,924 lots Friday to 200,869 contracts, continuing the decline from 18 month highs at 222,069 on July 16.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $328.50/25, compared to the London Monday afternoon fix at $325.75 and the New York close Friday around $325.75/25.

Gold prices have been consolidating in the past two weeks after hitting a 12 year low in early July around $314.00 an ounce, following confirmation of a sale of 167 tonnes of gold by the Australian central bank.

But rising gold production and producer hedging by Australian miners maybe weighing on the market also, traders said. Australian gold mine production for the June quarter 1997 was forecast to rise to a record 78 tonnes, mining consultants Surbiton Associates Pty Ltd said Monday.
The June quarter forecast output is about five tonnes more than in the March quarter and two tonnes above the record 75.8 tonnes in the December 1996 quarter, Surbiton said.
But physical gold demand is seen picking up again soon, with the start of the Hindu festival season in August, analysts said.

The monsoon has generally been good across India to date, for the eleventh year in a row so, and Indian farmers will soon be back in the market with the first earnings from the winter harvest, Bombay Bullion Association president Makhan Lal Damani said Monday.

With world jewellery and industrial demand for gold rising faster than mine supply, the supply/demand gap will continue to grow by about 100 tonnes a year, and will be filled in the short term by about 200 tonnes of producer hedging a year, and 300 tonnes of central banks sales, T. Hoare and Co analyst Rhona O'Connell told a South African mining conference Monday.
Meanwhile, COMEX September silver ended up 3.8 cents at $4.358 an ounce, with the September/December spread narrowing further to 5.5 cents.
September silver remains trapped in its $4.20-4.40 range, after spot silver saw three year lows earlier this month.

"In the last month, the two highest volume days in silver came on big washout days, while the lowest volume day came on the biggest attempt to rally, which even failed to hold on the day, and that tells us the trend is down," CRB analyst Terry Roggensack said.
Platinum group metals (PGM) prices continued to recover Monday from the two month lows seen in early July, despite the resumption of Russian exports in the past week.
NYMEX October platinum ended up $8.60 at $425.30 an ounce, with the October NYMEX platinum/COMEX gold spread climbing to $9.280 an ounce.
NYMEX September palladium ended up $3.95 at $193.60 an ounce, after seeing a new contract high at $195.00.
PGM futures on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) rose sharply again overnight to their highest levels in two months, helped by the stronger dollar/yen rate.
But news that Toyota Motor Corp plans to introduce low emission vehicle models later this year that will use more platinum group metals in their autocatalysts than existing models, also helped.

On the supply side, the first Russian shipments of palladium and platinum, under a new contract with Japanese trade houses, has now arrived in Japan, but reports overnight indicated no further metal was due to arrive in Japan under the contracts until August 7.
